specification.problem: Estimate the influence of each variable x_i on an n-variable Boolean function f using one-shot runs of the Bernstein-Vazirani circuit, where Pr[y_i=1] equals the influence of x_i on f.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Single construction: the standard Bernstein-Vazirani circuit applied to a generic f:{0,1}^n->{0,1}, with the per-position output probability Pr[y_i=1] identified with the influence, and a sampling estimator. Tiny instance: n=2, f(x)=x_1 AND x_2 (an assumption). Out of scope: the junta-learning algorithms, their complexity and speedup comparison against Floess et al., and the paper's own error analysis.

symbols.meaning: number of circuit runs for estimation

equations.label: Output distribution of BV circuit
equations.description: Measurement distribution after H^{\otimes n}, the phase oracle, then H^{\otimes n} on |0^n>.
equations.justification: Standard Fourier-sampling analysis of the Bernstein-Vazirani circuit; not stated in the abstract.
assumptions: Ancilla in |-> or equivalent phase kickback

equations.label: Influence definition
equations.description: Standard influence of variable x_i with x uniform on {0,1}^n.
equations.justification: The abstract equates the 'dependence degree' with the influence, but it does not give the formula; this is the standard definition.

equations.label: Probability of 1 at position i equals influence
equations.description: Marginal probability of a 1 in position i of the BV output equals the influence of x_i.
equations.abstract_quote: the probability of getting a 1 in each position $i$ is equal to the dependence degree of $f$ on the variable $x_{i}$, i.e. the influence of $x_{i}$ on $f$
equations.justification: The equality with influence is the abstract's claim. The middle expression follows from eq_1, and the equality with the influence definition is standard Fourier analysis.

equations.label: Sampling estimator
equations.description: Empirical frequency of 1s at position i over N independent runs, with a Hoeffding bound.
equations.abstract_quote: we give an approximation algorithm to evaluate the influence of any variable on a Boolean function
equations.justification: The approximation algorithm is presumed to be repeated sampling; the Hoeffding bound is a standard tool that I added, not the paper's own analysis.
assumptions: Paper's actual algorithm and error bound unknown

equations.label: Tiny instance
equations.description: For AND on 2 bits, (-1)^f has all four squared Fourier coefficients equal to 1/4, so each position is 1 with probability 1/2.
equations.justification: Chosen as a small checkable example; it is consistent with eq_2, since flipping x_i changes f for exactly half of the inputs.

registers.name: x
registers.role: input register, measured to give y; bit i corresponds to x_i (ordering assumed)

registers.name: anc
registers.role: phase-kickback ancilla in |-> (or use a direct phase oracle)

specification.initial_state: |0>^{\otimes n} on x, and |1> on anc (made into |-> by a Hadamard)

steps.description: Apply H^{\otimes n} to x and prepare the ancilla in |->.
Apply the oracle U_f: |x>|b> -> |x>|b xor f(x)>, which gives the phase (-1)^{f(x)} on x.
Apply H^{\otimes n} to x and measure it to obtain y.
Repeat N times and average the i-th bits to estimate the influence.

specification.measurement: Computational-basis measurement of the n-qubit input register; the ancilla is not measured.
specification.classical_postprocessing: For each i, compute the fraction of runs with y_i=1 as the influence estimate; the choice of N follows from the desired epsilon.
assumptions: Scope and the tiny instance (AND on 2 bits) are my own choices
Bit i of y corresponds to variable x_i
Hoeffding-based N is my addition, not from the abstract
missing_information: The paper's exact proof and formula for the dependence degree
The paper's approximation algorithm and its error and complexity bounds
The junta-learning algorithms and their success probabilities
Details of the speedup comparison against Floess et al.
